title: eddy-shift-scratch-dossier
content:
Purpose: quick, messy notes for Eddy shift (overnight). Not a canonical runbook — this is my brain-dump + short-term fixes and the things I usually forget when handing off.

Top-of-shift: 21:10
- Check dedupe alerts dashboard (Console > Alerts > dedupe). If spike, check prefix cache eviction rates.
- Check model-serving pods (kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=model-server). Note any CrashLoop or OOMKilled.
- Look at SLO panel: 95th latency, per-model.

Common problems and quick actions (do these first to buy time):
1) Model responses start returning truncated or repeated prefixes (likely KV-cache desync)
   - Symptoms: identical repeated tokens at beginning of generation; different responses vs previous commit for same prompt.
   - Quick mitigations:
     a) curl health endpoint of model-server to confirm worker cache sizes: 
        curl -sS http://model-server-qa.internal:8080/debug/cache | jq '.'  # look for negative seq ids
     b) Restart single worker to clear its in-memory KV cache (do one pod at a time):
        kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/model-server-<model>-worker-0 --grace-period=30  # note: replace <model>
     c) If issue persists across pods, restart the whole deployment with a staggered rolling restart.
   - Escalation: create a quick incident note in Slack channel and tag Marco. If we see >10% regression across traffic, fallback route to smaller-quantized model (route rule id: route-quant-slow-2025).

2) GPU OOM during batch ramp (common around mid-deploy autoscale window)
   - Symptoms: pod OOMKilled, logs show CUDA out-of-memory on batch step.
   - Quick mitigations:
     a) Temporarily reduce max_batch_size via dynamic config: POST to config svc: 
        curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"max_batch_size":16}' https://console.internal.redwood/api/runtime/config/model-<model>
     b) If config svc unavailable, scale down the replica count to reduce simultaneous batches: 
        kubectl -n inference scale deploy/model-server-<model> --replicas=2
     c) If ongoing OOMs, shift some traffic to a less memory-hungry model variant (model-v2-small). Update traffic rule in console or run: 
        ./scripts/switch-route.sh route-id=canary-<id> target=model-v2-small
n   - Notes: always annotate the action in #infra-ops and leave the rollback steps in the incident thread.

3) High tail latency / sudden latency spikes (could be noisy neighbor or network flakiness)
   - First-check: are all healthy nodes available (kubectl get nodes). If GCE/AWS node down, check cloud console.
   - If only one AZ impacted: reroute traffic to other regions (policy: latency-first failover).
   - Debugging commands: 
       kubectl -n inference top pod -l app=model-server  # look for CPU spikes
       curl -sS http://obs.internal/api/latency?window=5m&model=<model>
   - Temporary mitigation: throttle client-side concurrency via API gateway for that model (console: routes > edit > concurrency cap).

Quick CLI snippets I use (copy/paste with caution):
- kubectl -n inference get pods -l team=staging -o wide
- kubectl logs -n inference <pod> -c model-server --tail=200
- kubectl exec -it -n inference <pod> -- /bin/bash -c 'ps aux | grep model-server'
- gcloud compute ssh svc-runtime-1 --zone=us-west1-b -- 'sudo journalctl -u gpu-drivers -n 200'

Escalation contacts (fast path):
- oncall eng-sre primary: Marco Diaz (Slack @marco)
- secondary: Lena Chow (Slack @lena)
- SRE manager (for >30m outage): Aaron Mills

Notes to next shift: things I noticed but didn't fully triage
- 23:45 — small blip of 503s on model-batch-3, lasted ~2m, no pod restarts. Stack traces show transient Redis timeouts (INF-3421). Might be Redis high-latency; check redis-cluster-1 metrics and eviction.
- There's a flaky alert on 'inference:response-err-rate' that has been firing noisy for low volumes — filing a cleanup ticket tomorrow (tag: noise-alerts).

Temporary runbook fragment (for now, will formalize later):
- Redis/KV cache transient errors:
  1) Check redis latency: redis-cli -h redis-main.internal latency latest
  2) If latency > 30ms, switch to standby redis: ./tools/replica-switch redis-main -> redis-standby (ops script, needs sudo)
  3) If no standby available, set model runtime config "disable_prefix_cache": true for the affected model until Redis healthy.

Incident logging (what I do):
- Create quick incident note: https://docs.internal/incidents/new (use template "quick-night"), include: timestamps, actions, commands run, and who was notified.
- Put links to Slack thread + Jira INF-3421 in the note. Mark as "triaged" if resolved in <30m.

Personal TODOs (follow-up tomorrow):
- Look into noisy 'response-err-rate' alert: reduce sensitivity or add when:traffic-volume>100 rule.
- Add a small playbook for model cache desync to the shared runbooks (eng/sre/runbooks/cache-desync.md).
- Confirm standby redis auto-failover test schedule with infra team.

Random quick fixes I sometimes forget to mention:
- After a rolling restart, give pods ~2 minutes before invoking load tests — some worker processes do lazy JIT and initial requests will be slower.
- If you restart k8s pods and the deployment doesn't come back: check PVC mounts — sometimes CSI driver reconnect fails and containers go CrashLoopBackOff.

Questions for next-doc cleanup:
- Do we want to keep route-quant-slow-2025 as a permanent fallback? (Pros/cons: cost vs stability)
- Should we expose a lightweight cache-healthmetric per model to surface desync earlier?

Sign-off to next shift: please ping me on Slack if anything odd between 02:00-04:00 (I tend to be awake then). If you see repeated KV cache desyncs across >3 models, don't waste time restarting all pods — trigger the canary rollback to previous commit (rollback tag: v2025-01-29-stable).

Endnotes / logs I left during shift (timestamped):
- 21:23 - restarted worker model-server-nero-0 (cleared local cache), latency normalized.
- 23:44 - noted redis timeouts, added note to INF-3421.
- 00:04 - applied temporary max_batch_size reduction on model-aurora via config svc (reverted next morning).

That's it — messy but hopefully useful. If you're reading this and you find a repeated step you used, copy it to the canonical runbooks (eng/sre/runbooks).

--- Priya (eddy shift)
